chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Ibn Bukayr, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the one with incontinence, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'He continues upon his prayer.'

key_terms.الْمَبْطُونِ: One suffering from incontinence or continuous discharge of impurity
key_terms.يَبْنِي: He builds/continues (implies continuing the prayer without interruption or repetition)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for someone with incontinence regarding repeating prayers?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) establishes the ruling for *al-mabtoon* (one with continuous incontinence), clarifying that they perform a single prayer for each time period without needing to repeat wudu for every minor impurity, provided they maintain their state. This ruling highlights the principle of *al-‘urf* (customary practice) and ease in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing the *mabtoon* from the *mu’dhan* (one with intermittent incontinence) who must renew wudu for each prayer. It underscores the practical application of removing hardship (*raf’ al-haraj*) in daily worship.
